title: The US Army Looks to the Pacific – and Space – for Future Relevance
gist: The US Army is orienting toward the Pacific and space, drawing on lessons from the Middle East and Ukraine, to stay relevant as institutional emphasis shifts to long-range unmanned systems; the piece says the Navy and Air Force suffered setbacks in the war against Iran. Short excerpt only.

insights.claim: The US Army sees its future in preparing for a Pacific fight, drawing on lessons from the Middle East and Russia's war in Ukraine, with missiles, drones, electronic warfare and a growing space-domain role.
insights.speaker: Robert Farley
insights.so_what: Points to Army demand for drones, EW, missiles and space capabilities.

insights.claim: The author says the Navy suffered setbacks in the war against Iran from overcommitting its carrier fleet and the Air Force from losing several key assets, while the Army's contribution has been more limited, partly because the Trump administration has been reluctant to plan an invasion of Iran.
insights.speaker: Robert Farley
insights.so_what: Service-level setbacks may shape procurement priorities toward long-range unmanned systems.
insights.locator: Both the U.S. Navy and the U.S. Air Force
